```{r}
#| label: setup

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)

# ============================================================================
# CONFIG  --  edit between runs
# ============================================================================

# ---- Input -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Kinetics CSVs in the standard layout: first column = time in hours, then one
# column per well ("B2", "B3", ...). One file per fluorophore; the NAME of each
# entry is the fluorophore label used in titles and grouping.
infiles <- c(
  GFP = here("data", "processed", "2026", params$run,
             paste0(params$run, "_GFP_kinetics_raw.csv"))
)

# Two fluorophores would be:
# infiles <- c(
#   GFP     = here("data", "processed", "2026", "261111_EK",
#                  "261111_EK_GFP_kinetics_raw.csv"),
#   mCherry = here("data", "processed", "2026", "261111_EK",
#                  "261111_EK_mCherry_kinetics_raw.csv")
# )

# Name used in figure titles. NULL = the first file's name without extension.
dataset_label <- NULL

# ---- Blanks ----------------------------------------------------------------
# One entry per blank set. `blank` = the wells averaged per timepoint;
# `samples` = the wells that average is subtracted from. Any well spec works:
# "B2:B5", "B2,C2,D2", c("A1", "B3:B6"). Use samples = "rest" for every
# remaining non-blank well not claimed by another entry.
#
# A well is subtracted once, by the first entry that claims it. Blank wells
# themselves are never subtracted and are dropped from the grouped figures.
# Set blank_groups <- list() to skip blank subtraction entirely.
blank_groups <- list()

# blank_groups <- list(
#   list(blank = "B2:B5",  samples = "B6:B15, C2:C15"),
#   list(blank = "D2:D5",  samples = "rest")
# )

# Use blank-subtracted values in the grouped figures?
use_blank_subtraction <- FALSE

# ---- Display window --------------------------------------------------------
# Default hours of kinetics to show in the grouped figures. NULL or Inf = the
# whole run. Each figure has its own knob at the top of its chunk and falls
# back on this. The plate figure always shows the full run.
display_hours <- NULL

# Panels per row in the technical-replicate figure (NULL = ggplot decides)
technical_ncol <- NULL

# ---- Replicate structure ---------------------------------------------------
# ONE ROW PER BIOLOGICAL REPLICATE. Its `well_spec` lists the three technical
# replicate wells (a range "B2:B4", a list "B2,C2,D2", or both).
# well_spec is a STRING - quote it: "B2:D2", not B2:D2.
#
#   technical replicates  = the wells within one row
#   biological replicates = the rows sharing a `sample`
#
# Set to NULL to fall back on the auto_map() placeholder (consecutive triplets),
# which only exists so the document renders before the real design is entered.
sample_map <- tribble(
  ~sample,                   ~bio_rep, ~well_spec,

# ---- Plateau detection -----------------------------------------------------
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

# ============================================================================
# Well-ID machinery
# ============================================================================

parse_well <- function(w) {
  m <- str_match(toupper(trimws(w)), "^([A-P])\\s*(\\d{1,2})$")
  if (is.na(m[1, 1])) stop("Bad well ID: '", w, "'")
  c <- as.integer(m[1, 3])
  if (c < 1 || c > 24) stop("Column out of range (1-24) in well: '", w, "'")
  list(row = match(m[1, 2], LETTERS), col = c)
}

# Canonical, unpadded well ID: "B02" -> "B2"
norm_well <- function(w) {
  p <- parse_well(w)
  paste0(LETTERS[p$row], p$col)
}

# Expand well specs: wells("B2"), wells("A1:A4"), wells("B2:D4"),
# wells("A1, A2, B7"), wells(c("A1", "B3:B6"))
wells <- function(...) {
  specs <- unlist(list(...), use.names = FALSE)
  specs <- trimws(unlist(strsplit(specs, ","), use.names = FALSE))
  specs <- specs[nzchar(specs)]

  out <- character(0)
  for (s in specs) {
    if (grepl(":", s, fixed = TRUE)) {
      parts <- strsplit(s, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      if (length(parts) != 2) stop("Bad well range: '", s, "'")
      a <- parse_well(parts[1]); b <- parse_well(parts[2])
      rr <- seq(min(a$row, b$row), max(a$row, b$row))
      cc <- seq(min(a$col, b$col), max(a$col, b$col))
      out <- c(out, paste0(rep(LETTERS[rr], each = length(cc)),
                           rep(cc, times = length(rr))))
    } else {
      out <- c(out, norm_well(s))
    }
  }
  unique(out)
}

order_wells <- function(ws) {
  ws[order(match(substr(ws, 1, 1), LETTERS), as.integer(substring(ws, 2)))]
}

well_row <- function(ws) factor(substr(ws, 1, 1), levels = LETTERS[1:16])
well_col <- function(ws) as.integer(substring(ws, 2))

# ============================================================================
# Reader
# ============================================================================

# Standard kinetics CSV: first column = time in hours, then one column per
# well. Returns a long tibble: fluorophore | well | time_h | value_raw.
# `paths` is a NAMED vector - the names become the fluorophore labels.
read_kinetics <- function(paths) {
  if (is.null(names(paths)) || any(!nzchar(names(paths)))) {
    stop("`infiles` must be a named vector, e.g. c(GFP = \"path/to/file.csv\")")
  }

  imap_dfr(paths, function(path, fluoro) {
    if (!file.exists(path)) stop("File not found: ", path)

    raw <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    if (ncol(raw) < 2) stop("Expected a time column plus well columns in ",
                            basename(path))

    tcol <- names(raw)[1]
    if (!str_detect(tcol, regex("^time", ignore_case = TRUE))) {
      warning("First column of ", basename(path), " is '", tcol,
              "' - treating it as time in hours.")
    }
    names(raw)[1] <- "time_h"

    bad <- setdiff(names(raw)[-1],
                   names(raw)[-1][str_detect(names(raw)[-1],
                                             "^[A-Pa-p]\\s*\\d{1,2}$")])
    if (length(bad) > 0) {
      stop("Column name(s) in ", basename(path),
           " are not well IDs: ", paste(head(bad, 8), collapse = ", "))
    }

    raw %>%
      pivot_longer(-time_h, names_to = "well", values_to = "value_raw") %>%
      mutate(
        well        = vapply(well, norm_well, character(1)),
        time_h      = as.numeric(time_h),
        value_raw   = as.numeric(value_raw),
        fluorophore = fluoro
      )
  }) %>%
    select(fluorophore, well, time_h, value_raw)
}

# ============================================================================
# Blank subtraction (per timepoint, per fluorophore, per blank set)
# ============================================================================

is_rest <- function(x) {
  is.character(x) && length(x) == 1 && tolower(trimws(x)) == "rest"
}

spec_wells <- function(x) if (is.null(x) || is_rest(x)) character(0) else wells(x)

# All wells used as blanks, across every entry
blank_wells_of <- function(groups) {
  unique(unlist(lapply(groups, function(g) spec_wells(g$blank))))
}

# well -> blank-set index. First entry wins; one "rest" entry mops up.
blank_assignment <- function(groups, all_wells) {
  bl <- intersect(blank_wells_of(groups), all_wells)
  out <- tibble(well = character(), blank_set = integer())
  claimed <- character(0)

  for (i in seq_along(groups)) {
    tg <- setdiff(intersect(spec_wells(groups[[i]]$samples), all_wells), bl)
    dup <- intersect(tg, claimed)
    if (length(dup) > 0) {
      warning("Wells claimed by more than one blank set, first wins: ",
              paste(head(dup, 8), collapse = ", "))
      tg <- setdiff(tg, claimed)
    }
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(well = tg, blank_set = i))
    claimed <- c(claimed, tg)
  }

  rest <- which(vapply(groups, function(g) is_rest(g$samples), logical(1)))
  if (length(rest) > 1) warning("More than one 'rest' blank set - using the first.")
  if (length(rest) >= 1) {
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(well = setdiff(all_wells, c(claimed, bl)),
                                 blank_set = rest[1]))
  }
  out
}

subtract_blanks <- function(d, groups) {
  if (length(groups) == 0) {
    return(mutate(d, value = value_raw, blank_set = NA_integer_))
  }
  all_wells <- unique(d$well)

  missing <- setdiff(blank_wells_of(groups), all_wells)
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    warning("Blank wells not in the data (ignored): ",
            paste(head(missing, 8), collapse = ", "))
  }

  blank_vals <- map_dfr(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
    bw <- intersect(spec_wells(groups[[i]]$blank), all_wells)
    if (length(bw) == 0) return(tibble())
    d %>%
      filter(well %in% bw) %>%
      group_by(fluorophore, time_h) %>%
      summarise(blank = mean(value_raw, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(blank_set = i)
  })

  d %>%
    left_join(blank_assignment(groups, all_wells), by = "well") %>%
    left_join(blank_vals, by = c("fluorophore", "time_h", "blank_set")) %>%
    mutate(value = value_raw - coalesce(blank, 0)) %>%
    select(-blank)
}

# ============================================================================
# Replicate map
# ============================================================================

# PLACEHOLDER: chop a well selection into consecutive triplets (one triplet =
# one biological replicate), then group `bio_per_sample` triplets per sample.
auto_map <- function(ws, bio_per_sample = auto_bio_per_sample,
                     sample_names = NULL) {
  ws <- order_wells(ws)
  usable <- (length(ws) %/% 3) * 3
  if (usable < length(ws)) {
    warning("auto_map(): ", length(ws) - usable,
            " well(s) dropped - not a multiple of three.")
    ws <- ws[seq_len(usable)]
  }
  trip  <- split(ws, ceiling(seq_along(ws) / 3))
  s_idx <- ceiling(seq_along(trip) / bio_per_sample)
  if (is.null(sample_names)) sample_names <- sprintf("grp%02d", seq_len(max(s_idx)))
  tibble(
    sample    = sample_names[s_idx],
    bio_rep   = unlist(lapply(rle(s_idx)$lengths, seq_len), use.names = FALSE),
    well_spec = vapply(trip, paste, character(1), collapse = ",")
  )
}

# Catch the map mistakes that would otherwise regroup wells silently
check_map <- function(m) {
  need <- c("sample", "bio_rep", "well_spec")
  if (!all(need %in% names(m))) {
    stop("sample_map needs columns: ", paste(need, collapse = ", "),
         ". Found: ", paste(names(m), collapse = ", "),
         " (a repeated ~sample, ~bio_rep, ~well_spec header line does this).")
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(names(m))) {
    stop("sample_map has duplicate column names - check for a repeated ",
         "~sample, ~bio_rep, ~well_spec header line.")
  }

  dup <- m %>% count(sample, bio_rep) %>% filter(n > 1)
  if (nrow(dup) > 0) {
    warning("sample_map: same sample + bio_rep on more than one row, their ",
            "wells are pooled - ",
            paste(sprintf("%s rep %s", dup$sample, dup$bio_rep),
                  collapse = "; "))
  }

  e <- expand_map(m)
  shared <- e %>% count(well) %>% filter(n > 1)
  if (nrow(shared) > 0) {
    warning("sample_map: well(s) listed in more than one entry - ",
            paste(head(order_wells(shared$well), 8), collapse = ", "))
  }
  invisible(m)
}

# map (one row per biological replicate) -> one row per well, with tech_rep
expand_map <- function(m) {
  m %>%
    mutate(.row = row_number()) %>%
    rowwise(.row) %>%
    mutate(well = list(wells(well_spec))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    unnest(well) %>%
    group_by(sample, bio_rep) %>%
    mutate(tech_rep = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(sample, bio_rep, tech_rep, well)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: load

dataset <- dataset_label %||%
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(infiles[[1]]))

blank_well_ids <- blank_wells_of(blank_groups)

# Subtraction only happens if it is switched on AND blank sets exist
blanks_applied <- use_blank_subtraction && length(blank_groups) > 0

# ---- Read + blank-subtract -------------------------------------------------
dat <- read_kinetics(infiles) %>% subtract_blanks(blank_groups)

# ---- Replicate structure ---------------------------------------------------
map_is_auto <- is.null(sample_map)
map_used <- if (map_is_auto) {
  auto_map(setdiff(unique(dat$well), blank_well_ids))
} else {
  check_map(sample_map)
}

dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(expand_map(map_used), by = "well") %>%
  mutate(
    plate_row = well_row(well),
    plate_col = well_col(well),
    is_blank  = well %in% blank_well_ids,
    value_use = if (blanks_applied) value else value_raw,
    rep_id    = paste0(sample, " r", bio_rep, ".", tech_rep)
  )

value_label <- if (blanks_applied) {
  "Fluorescence, blank-subtracted (a.u.)"
} else {
  "Fluorescence, raw (a.u.)"
}

# Wells in the data that the map says nothing about
unmapped <- dat %>% filter(!is_blank, is.na(sample)) %>% distinct(well) %>% pull(well)
if (length(unmapped) > 0) {
  warning(length(unmapped), " well(s) in the data are not in sample_map and are ",
          "left out of the grouped figures: ",
          paste(head(order_wells(unmapped), 8), collapse = ", "))
}

# Wells the map expects but the file does not contain
missing_wells <- setdiff(expand_map(map_used)$well, unique(dat$well))
if (length(missing_wells) > 0) {
  warning(length(missing_wells), " well(s) in sample_map are not in the data: ",
          paste(head(order_wells(missing_wells), 8), collapse = ", "))
}

# Cut a tibble to a display window; NULL/Inf keeps everything
window_hours <- function(d, hours) {
  if (is.null(hours) || !is.finite(hours)) d else filter(d, time_h <= hours)
}
```

## 1. Individual traces, in plate position

Every measured well in its own panel, arranged as on the plate. Raw values, so
plate-level artefacts (edge effects, a dead well, a bubble) stay visible. Blank
wells are drawn in orange.

```{r}
#| label: plate-traces
#| fig-height: 8

plot_plate <- function(d) {
  ggplot(d, aes(time_h, value_raw, group = well, colour = is_blank)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
    facet_grid(plate_row ~ plate_col) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = okabe_ito[1], `TRUE` = okabe_ito[2]),
                        labels = c(`FALSE` = "sample", `TRUE` = "blank"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(3)) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(dataset, " - ", unique(d$fluorophore), " - individual wells"),
      x = "Time (h)", y = "Fluorescence, raw (a.u.)"
    )
}

for (d in group_split(dat, fluorophore)) print(plot_plate(d))
```

## 2. Plateau times

Each well is smoothed with a centred rolling mean over `r plateau_smooth_k`
points; the plateau is the first timepoint at which the smoothed trace reaches
`r scales::percent(plateau_frac)` of its own smoothed maximum. A well that never
rises (flat or noise-only) gives a meaningless early time, so check `rise`
before trusting a row. Times come from the full run, not the display window.

```{r}
#| label: plateau

# Samples excluded from plateau analysis (regex on the sample name).
# They stay in the figures as controls, they just don't get plateau numbers.
# NULL = keep everything.

plateau_exclude <- "noDNA"

roll_mean <- function(x, k) {
  if (k <= 1) return(x)
  n <- length(x)
  half <- (k - 1) %/% 2
  vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    idx <- max(1, i - half):min(n, i + half)
    mean(x[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))
}

plateau_of <- function(time_h, value, frac = plateau_frac, k = plateau_smooth_k) {
  ok <- !is.na(value)
  if (sum(ok) < 3) return(tibble(t_plateau = NA_real_, v_plateau = NA_real_,
                                 rise = NA_real_))
  tt <- time_h[ok]; vv <- roll_mean(value[ok], k)
  v0 <- min(vv); vmax <- max(vv)
  hit <- which(vv >= v0 + frac * (vmax - v0))
  i <- if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_integer_
  tibble(t_plateau = if (is.na(i)) NA_real_ else tt[i],
         v_plateau = if (is.na(i)) NA_real_ else vv[i],
         rise      = vmax - v0)
}

plateau_well <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample), !is_blank,
         if (is.null(plateau_exclude)) TRUE else !str_detect(sample, plateau_exclude)) %>%
  group_by(fluorophore, sample, bio_rep, tech_rep, well) %>%
  reframe(plateau_of(time_h, value_use)) %>%
  filter(is.na(rise) | rise >= plateau_min_rise)

plateau_well <- plateau_well %>%
  mutate(across(c(t_plateau, v_plateau, rise), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  arrange(sample, bio_rep, tech_rep)

# Mean +/- SD across the technical replicates of each biological replicate
plateau_tech <- plateau_well %>%
  group_by(fluorophore, sample, bio_rep) %>%
  summarise(n          = sum(!is.na(t_plateau)),
            mean_t     = mean(t_plateau, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_t       = sd(t_plateau, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_level = mean(v_plateau, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_level   = sd(v_plateau, na.rm = TRUE),
            cv_level   = 100 * sd(v_plateau, na.rm = TRUE) /
                               mean(v_plateau, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

# Mean +/- SD across biological replicates (each one its technical mean).
# Rename first: summarise() would otherwise read the mean_t it just created.
plateau_bio <- plateau_tech %>%
  rename(t_rep = mean_t, level_rep = mean_level) %>%
  group_by(fluorophore, sample) %>%
  summarise(n          = sum(!is.na(t_rep)),
            mean_t     = mean(t_rep, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_t       = sd(t_rep, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_level = mean(level_rep, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_level   = sd(level_rep, na.rm = TRUE),
            cv_level   = 100 * sd(level_rep, na.rm = TRUE) /
                               mean(level_rep, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

One row per well. `t_` columns are hours, `f_` columns are fluorescence at the
plateau in the same units as the traces. `_well` is that well; `_tech` is the
mean over the three technical replicates of its biological replicate; `_bio` is
the mean over the biological replicates of its sample.

```{r}
#| label: plateau-table

plateau_table <- plateau_well %>%
  select(fluorophore, well, sample, tech_rep, bio_rep,
         t_well = t_plateau, f_well = v_plateau) %>%
  left_join(plateau_tech %>%
              select(fluorophore, sample, bio_rep,
                     t_tech = mean_t, f_tech = mean_level, cv_tech = cv_level),
            by = c("fluorophore", "sample", "bio_rep")) %>%
  left_join(plateau_bio %>%
              select(fluorophore, sample,
                     t_bio = mean_t, f_bio = mean_level, cv_bio = cv_level),
            by = c("fluorophore", "sample")) %>%
  arrange(sample, bio_rep, tech_rep)

# Drop the fluorophore column when there is only one in the data
if (n_distinct(plateau_table$fluorophore) == 1) {
  plateau_table <- select(plateau_table, -fluorophore)
}

# A real table: searchable, sortable, paged - in the editor preview and in the
# rendered HTML alike. (A bare tibble only becomes a table on render, and only
# because of df-print.)
show_table <- function(d, page = 25) {
  if (requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)) {
    DT::datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                  extensions = "Buttons",
                  options = list(pageLength = page, scrollX = TRUE,
                                 scrollY = "420px", scrollCollapse = TRUE,
                                 dom = "Bfrtip",
                                 buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel")))
  } else {
    warning("Install DT for a proper table: install.packages(\"DT\")")
    print(as.data.frame(d))
  }
}

show_table(plateau_table)
```

## 3. Technical replicates

One panel per biological replicate: its three technical replicate wells as thin
lines, with the per-timepoint **mean ± SD** across them. `tech_hours` at the top
of the chunk cuts the x-axis (`NULL` = the `display_hours` default from setup);
`technical_ncol` controls the panel grid.

```{r}
#| label: technical-traces
#| fig-height: 7

# Hours to display in THIS figure. NULL = use display_hours from setup.
tech_hours <- NULL

dat_tech <- window_hours(dat, tech_hours %||% display_hours)

tech_sum <- dat_tech %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample), !is_blank) %>%
  group_by(fluorophore, sample, bio_rep, time_h) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(value_use, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd  = sd(value_use, na.rm = TRUE),
            n   = sum(!is.na(value_use)), .groups = "drop")

plot_technical <- function(d) {
  s <- filter(tech_sum, fluorophore == unique(d$fluorophore))
  ggplot(s, aes(time_h, avg)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = avg - sd, ymax = avg + sd),
                fill = okabe_ito[1], alpha = 0.20) +
    geom_line(data = d, aes(y = value_use, group = well),
              colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_line(colour = okabe_ito[1], linewidth = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ sample + bio_rep, ncol = technical_ncol,
               labeller = labeller(.multi_line = FALSE)) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(dataset, " - ", unique(d$fluorophore),
                     " - technical replicates (mean +/- SD)"),
      x = "Time (h)", y = value_label
    )
}

for (d in group_split(filter(dat_tech, !is.na(sample), !is_blank), fluorophore)) {
  print(plot_technical(d))
}
```

## 4. Biological replicates

Each biological replicate is first collapsed to one trace (mean of its three
technical replicates). Those traces are the thin lines; the band is the
per-timepoint **mean ± SD** across biological replicates. `bio_hours` at the top
of the chunk sets this figure's window independently of section 3.

```{r}
#| label: biological-traces
#| fig-height: 6

# Hours to display in THIS figure. NULL = use display_hours from setup.
bio_hours <- NULL

bio_trace <- window_hours(dat, bio_hours %||% display_hours) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample), !is_blank) %>%
  group_by(fluorophore, sample, bio_rep, time_h) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(value_use, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

bio_sum <- bio_trace %>%
  group_by(fluorophore, sample, time_h) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd  = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            n   = sum(!is.na(value)), .groups = "drop")

plot_biological <- function(d) {
  s <- filter(bio_sum, fluorophore == unique(d$fluorophore))
  ggplot(s, aes(time_h, avg)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = avg - sd, ymax = avg + sd),
                fill = okabe_ito[1], alpha = 0.20) +
    geom_line(data = d, aes(y = value, colour = factor(bio_rep),
                            group = bio_rep), linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_line(colour = okabe_ito[1], linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ sample) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = okabe_ito, name = "bio rep") +
    labs(
      title = paste0(dataset, " - ", unique(d$fluorophore),
                     " - biological replicates (mean +/- SD)"),
      x = "Time (h)", y = value_label
    )
}

for (d in group_split(bio_trace, fluorophore)) print(plot_biological(d))
```

```{r}
#| label: renv-status
#| code-fold: false

# renv::status() rescans every file in the project on each render, which is slow
# in a project that also holds data. This reads the lockfile instead and compares
# it with the packages this report actually attached - instant, and it is the
# part that matters for reproducing these figures.

renv_report <- function() {
  if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) {
    return("renv is not installed for this project. Run renv::init() to start.")
  }
  lock_path <- renv::paths$lockfile()
  if (!file.exists(lock_path)) return(paste("No lockfile at", lock_path))

  recorded <- tryCatch(renv::lockfile_read(lock_path)$Packages,
                       error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(recorded)) return(paste("Could not read", lock_path))

  attached <- sub("^package:", "", grep("^package:", search(), value = TRUE))

  # Drop everything that ships with R - renv never records these
base_pkgs <- rownames(installed.packages(priority = c("base", "recommended")))
attached <- setdiff(attached, base_pkgs)

  tibble(
    package  = attached,
    loaded   = vapply(attached,
                      function(p) as.character(utils::packageVersion(p)),
                      character(1)),
    lockfile = vapply(attached,
                      function(p) if (is.null(recorded[[p]])) NA_character_
                                  else recorded[[p]]$Version,
                      character(1))
  ) %>%
    mutate(status = case_when(is.na(lockfile)     ~ "not recorded",
                              loaded == lockfile  ~ "ok",
                              TRUE                ~ "differs")) %>%
    arrange(status != "ok", package)
}

res <- renv_report()
if (is.character(res)) cat(res, "\n") else show_table(res, page = 15)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Keeping the environment reproducible

A `not recorded` or `differs` row means the lockfile does not describe the
library this report just ran against. Fix it in the console, not here:
`renv::snapshot()` records what is installed now, `renv::restore()` rolls the
library back to the lockfile. Commit `renv.lock` alongside this `.qmd`.

For the full picture (including packages used but not attached here) run
`renv::status()` in the console. It scans every file in the project, so add a
`.renvignore` with `data/`, `*_files/` and `*_cache/` to keep that scan to your
sources rather than the data files.
:::
